I've farmed these 20 mu in Quzhou for 40 years. My old man taught me, and I finished middle school, so I can read the fertilizer bags and do the cost sums myself. But I still trust my eyes and what my neighbors do more than anything from a book. I have six people under my roof, including my sons who help in the fields, so we have the hands for intensive crops.

It is March now. My wheat is already in on 12 mu — I planted Jimai 26 last October, an improved variety that my neighbor Lao Zhang switched to three years ago. His wheat stood better than mine did, so I copied him and it worked. The wheat is greening up now. I pump from my well to water it three times: now at revival, again at jointing, and once more at grain filling. Last fall I put down 80 jin of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer per mu. This spring I top dress with 30 jin urea at green-up and another 20 jin at jointing. That comes to about 16 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 6 kg potassium per mu. I spray twice — once for aphids when they show up, and once for fungus if the weather turns wet. I expect 520 kg per mu. I will not cut back on fertilizer to save money. Lao Wang tried that last year and his wheat was thin as straw. A bad harvest is a disaster; wasting some fertilizer is just a cost.

After I harvest the wheat in early June, I rotary till that same 12 mu and plant Zhengdan 958 hybrid maize. Everyone here plants it. The seed dealer always stocks it, and the stalks don't fall over in wind. I put 80 jin of compound fertilizer in the planting furrow, then top dress with 25 jin urea at the big trumpet stage. That's 14 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium per mu. Two well waterings should do, three if July is bone dry. Two pesticide sprays. If the weather is normal I get 600 kg per mu.

The other 8 mu I split: 4 mu chili and 4 mu cotton. Chili brings better money but it needs more work and more inputs. I plough deep for chili, down 25 cm, and add farmyard manure plus 100 jin compound fertilizer and 60 jin potassium sulfate per mu. The dealer told me chili eats potassium for the fruit set, and I saw it work on Lao Li's field. That is 20 kg nitrogen, 8 kg phosphorus, and 15 kg potassium per mu. Five irrigations from the well, and six pesticide sprays because chili gets spider mites and virus disease easily. I hope for 2800 kg of fresh chili per mu.

Cotton is Bt hybrid — saves me labor on bollworm. I plough, put 80 jin compound fertilizer and some extra potassium at planting, then top dress twice. That is 12 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 8 kg potassium per mu. Four irrigations and four pesticide sprays for aphids and wilt. Last year I got 320 kg seed cotton per mu, and I will do the same again this year.

Everything connects in my pocket. A 50 kg bag of urea is over 100 yuan now, compound is 150 yuan. With 20 mu I spend thousands on fertilizer alone. But I have 20 mu, I can absorb some risk, and I would rather put in a bit too much than risk losing yield. A bad harvest means borrowing money or eating into savings. Extra fertilizer is just a few hundred yuan more.
